_comment: Judgment calls an unattended run must NOT make on its own, and must NOT block on either. Contract 3.6 appends here instead of halting; the run ships everything else and surfaces these in the briefing. P-funk reviews at leisure and resolves by editing the entry's status to 'resolved' with a note. Nothing in this file gates the pipeline. See SKILL.md Contract 3.6.

decisions.question: SKILL.md hard-coded SENATE_I = 3, counting Murkowski as an independent. senate.gov lists 2 (Sanders, King) and carries Murkowski as R, as does this dashboard's own Senate tab. Change the value and the skill, or keep 3?
decisions.why_not_autonomous: Contradicting an explicit hard-coded value in the canonical skill is a scope change, not a data update. The invariant SENATE_R + SENATE_D == 100 held either way, so nothing was blocked by deferring it.
decisions.resolution: Corrected to 2 on 2026-08-03 at P-funk's direction. SKILL.md 2.3 rewritten, corrections.json entry added, patch updated before the apply job ran.

decisions.question: The MO-05 row carries Party 'D' (Cleaver) with Rating 'Solid R' and a Note saying the Solid R label 'was sheet error'. Post-redistricting Solid R may be correct for the new seat, but the note and the cell contradict each other. Which is right?
decisions.why_not_autonomous: Resolving it means deciding whether the note or the rating is the stale artifact. I found no primary source settling it, and guessing would either restore a real error or erase a real correction.
options: Rating is right, delete the note
Note is right, rating should be D-favorable
Re-research the post-redistricting MO-05 partisan lean
decisions.resolution: Resolved 2026-08-03: the RATING was right and the NOTE was wrong. The note assumed a Democratic incumbent implies a Democratic-leaning rating, but a rating describes the seat. Missouri's mid-decade map turned MO-05 from Harris +24 into Trump 58-40 (Cook PVI R+9; Inside Elections Baseline R+17), and all three forecasters independently moved it to Safe/Solid R. Party cell stays D, Rating stays Solid R, note replaced with sourced reasoning. One live contingency recorded: a People Not Politicians referendum (~300k signatures, certification decision expected around the Aug 4 primary) could suspend the map, in which case the old lines would make this Solid D again.

decisions.question: Inside Elections uses a finer scale than the dashboard: it has a 'Tilt' tier between 'Lean' and 'Toss-up' (Toss-up / Tilt / Lean / Likely / Solid). The dashboard's 7-point enum has no 'Tilt'. On Aug 6, 2026 Inside Elections moved several races to a 'Tilt' rating (NC-Sen and GA-Sen to Tilt D, IA-Sen to Tilt R, KS-Gov to Tilt R, IA-Gov to Tilt D). How should an IE 'Tilt D/R' be represented on the 7-point sheet when it is the mover — collapse to 'Toss-up', collapse to 'Lean', or keep tracking Cook/Sabato (which share the 7-point scale) and treat IE only as corroboration?
decisions.why_not_autonomous: This is a standing methodology choice about which forecaster(s) the Rating column tracks and how to collapse a 5-gradation scale into 7 points, not a one-off data update. Picking a rule unilaterally would silently change how every future IE 'Tilt' move is handled.
options: Keep tracking Cook/Sabato on the 7-point scale; use IE only as corroboration (never import a bare 'Tilt')
Map IE 'Tilt D/R' to 'Toss-up' (Tilt is the most competitive non-tossup tier)
Map IE 'Tilt D/R' to 'Lean D/R' (nearest same-direction label)

decisions.question: The Senate ratings tab lists MT as incumbent Steve Daines (R) vs. Reilly Neill (D), Solid R. The State News pass (Montana Free Press, Daily Montanan) and news_config.json both indicate Daines did NOT seek re-election, Neill lost the June 2 Democratic primary to Alani Bankhead, and the November matchup is Kurt Alme (R) vs. Alani Bankhead (D) vs. independent Seth Bodnar. Should the Senate row's Incumbent/Challenger cells be rewritten to the Alme/Bankhead/Bodnar matchup (with Daines removed as incumbent)?
decisions.why_not_autonomous: This is a member-level/incumbent correction surfaced only by a news-gathering subagent, not the gating Contract 3.5 membership verifier. Rewriting the Incumbent cell (a field outside the normal rating row_update) on a single unverified pass risks a half-correct row. The rating is Solid R either way, so nothing is blocked by deferring; the State News tab already shows the correct current matchup.
options: Have next week's membership verifier confirm Daines retired, then rewrite Incumbent + Challenger together
Rewrite the matchup now to Alme (R) / Bankhead (D) / Bodnar (I)
Leave as-is pending a primary source
